Why is Saturn less dense than water?
it is made mostly of the lightest elements, H & He
it is made of frozen water ice

slides.reveal: Answer: A. Saturn is made mostly of hydrogen and helium, the two lightest elements, and it is not massive enough to squeeze them as much as Jupiter does, so its mean density (687 kg per cubic meter) is below water's (1,000).

What makes Jupiter's strong magnetic field?
spinning liquid metallic hydrogen deep inside
a giant iron bar magnet at its center
the solar wind blowing past it

slides.reveal: Answer: A. Jupiter's fast spin (about 10 hours) stirs its deep layer of liquid metallic hydrogen, which conducts electricity, and the moving currents make the magnetic field (a dynamo; slides 4 and 10).

Which clue best shows Triton was captured?

slides.reveal: Answer: A. Moons that form around a planet orbit in the same direction the planet spins; Triton's retrograde orbit is the strongest evidence that it formed elsewhere (probably in the Kuiper Belt) and was captured (slide 22).
